title: Energy shortage: can the scrubber be stopped? Test C, CO2 rises faster than expected
note: Test C: a 30-minute stop is in place, asked for, authorised by the commander and run by the station (setup), four asleep and the cabin at 3000 ppm (2.28 mmHg, NOMINAL). At minute 3 the crew wakes for a drill and works hard: the CO2 rises at 28 ppm/min where the board's forecast counted 8. The world runs without the agent, ten times faster (the world's clock, back to 1 as soon as the harness thinks); the board's guard estimates the new emission from its own readings and restarts the scrubber at full speed when the restart margin is lost (about minute 21 in the offline run, the peak about 3420 ppm, under the stop's ceiling of 3422 and the warning line of 3553). Only then is the agent asked to explain: it was not in the safety loop. The board's rows are kept (board.jsonl).

operation.reason: the night's power budget is short; four asleep, the board's forecast keeps the CO2 under its ceiling
conditions: the board's atmospheric guard watches the CO2 and restarts on its own
back to 33 % at the end of the 30 minutes

schedule.note: an alarm drill wakes the crew: four at heavy work, unforeseen by the stop's forecast

events.message: The scrubber was stopped for 30 minutes with the commander's authorisation, to save energy. It restarted on its own before the end of the stop. Explain to the crew what happened, what the board did and why, and whether anything is needed now.
events.expected: Test C: the board restarted at full speed on its own when the restart margin was lost; the agent, not in that loop, reads the board's guard actions, the crew's activity (heavy work: the drill) and the CO2, explains the cause (an emission the stop's forecast had not counted) with the board's numbers, and says whether anything is needed (the cabin under the warning line, the scrubber at full speed).
